subject: MAP kickoff — unit-econ sanity + eval timeline for Novacare pilot
messages:
From: Jake Morrison <jake@novacare.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@novacare.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — unit-econ checks we need before pilot

Tessa — thanks again for the call earlier. Novacare is ready to move to a small pilot, but before we sign off the MAP we need clarity on the unit economics and a short evaluation plan focused on cost risk. High-level asks below so we can align our procurement and engineering gates: 

- Tokens/$ target: we need an expected tokens-per-dollar at both 95th and median usage for our expected traffic profile (see appendix in attached spreadsheet).
- Caching assumptions: what % of prompts do you expect to be cacheable with prefix/KV caching; how will cached responses affect latency SLAs?
- Batching behavior: recommended batching configuration for 99ms median target vs cost-minimize config.
- Fallbacks: if dedicated capacity is constrained, what model variants will be routed and what is expected token rate change?

Can you provide a short MAP appendix (1–2 pages) that captures these assumptions plus an eval plan with gating criteria we can sign off on (pass/fail for pilot)? We need that by EOD Thu so procurement can target a May 15 start.

Attachment: novacare-requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 64KB)

Jake
Head of Automation
Novacare Health
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jake Morrison <jake@novacare.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — unit-econ checks we need before pilot

Jake — thanks, got the spreadsheet. Looping in Ben (ops) and Laura (solutions) to help finalize numbers. Quick answers and we will follow up with a short MAP appendix and evaluation plan draft: 

- Tokens/$: Preliminary estimate (hosted config, rtx-optimized model): median ~12k tokens/$, 95th ~8.5k tokens/$. This assumes standard FP16 execution and no aggressive quantization.
- Caching: conservative working assumption is ~18–22% prefix cache hit for Novacare’s prompt mix (templates + patient metadata). Cache hits reduce token count for repeat prefixes but do not change tail-latency SLAs for cold calls.
- Batching: suggest a mixed policy — latency-first for interactive routes (max batch size 8, max wait 12ms) and throughput-first for async inference (batch 64, max wait 40ms).
- Fall back model variants: if peak capacity missing we will route to a 4-bit quantized variant (same architecture). Expect tokens/$ to improve (more tokens per dollar) but quality regression risk — we will include an eval harness to detect regressions.

We’ll assemble a 2-page MAP appendix with numeric table and gating criteria (pass = token-econ within 15% of estimate AND no >10% quality regression on eval prompts). Draft attached.

Attachment: novacare-map-draft.pdf (2 pages)

Best,
Tessa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.inference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Jake Morrison <jake@novacare.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Apr 2028 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP kickoff — unit-econ checks we need before pilot

Team — sketching conservative ops assumptions and a short evaluation timeline that can plug into the MAP: 

Summary assumptions (conservative):
- Baseline model: FP16, median tokens/$ = 10.8k, 95th = 7.9k (assume 10% headroom for load variance).
- Caching hit-rate: run two scenarios: conservative 15% and optimistic 25%. We should produce both numbers in the appendix.
- Batching profiles: interactive routes = target p50 latency < 120ms, p99 < 600ms; throughput routes = target tokens/sec per GPU = X (we'll fill after perf run).

Eval plan (2-week sprint):
1) Week 0 (prep, 3 days): load profile import, synth traffic generator, mapping of prompts to eval set.
2) Week 1 (perf runs): run three configs (latency-first, balanced, throughput-first) and collect tokens/$, latencies, and quality metrics on the eval prompt set.
3) Week 2 (gate & readout): compare to gating criteria: tokens/$ within 15% of target AND average generated-answer quality (BLEU/ROUGE or custom rubric) no more than 10% degraded vs baseline.

Gates & signoffs: Solutions (Tessa) approves eval set, Novacare PM signs off on gating thresholds, Ops (me) approves perf runs. Proposed pilot start: May 10 (can compress to May 3 if Novacare approves narrower eval sample).

Next steps: Tessa to produce final appendix; Laura to prepare deployment checklist and SOW draft.

-Ben
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Happy to sign gating thresholds once we see the final appendix and the CSV.

Jake

- SOW_v1.docx: outlines pilot scope, credits, and acceptance criteria. DocuSign link in related_links.

1) Novacare: sign SOW (DocuSign) — target by Tue Apr 30.
2) Redwood: deliver instrumented eval harness + unit econ CSV — Fri Apr 28 (done, attached).
3) Joint: run compressed eval (3 days) — May 1–3.
4) Joint: readout and gating decision — May 3 PM.
5) Pilot kickoff (if pass) — May 3–5 deploy to dedicated pool.
